name: 90/10 Strategy (T-Bills Plus Long Calls)
summary: Put roughly 90% of capital in short-dated Treasuries and spend the interest (and only the interest) on long calls - a whole-portfolio allocation whose worst case is a small, known haircut.

legs.strike_rule: 90-95% of capital into SGOV or BIL (the T-bill sleeve; share counts vary with price)
legs.dte_rule: held continuously, rolled by the fund

legs.strike_rule: ATM to slightly OTM, call delta 0.45-0.60, on SPY or QQQ; contract count set so total premium <= the sleeve's expected interest over the option's life

max_profit: UNLIMITED - full delta participation above the call strike, plus the T-bill interest
max_loss: The call premium spent, i.e. approximately one period's interest; the T-bill sleeve itself is not at market risk beyond a few days of duration
breakevens: call strike + premium per share, ignoring the interest offset; with the interest counted, the portfolio breaks even flat

greeks.delta: +45 to +60 per call contract; the T-bill sleeve is delta-flat
greeks.theta: negative on the calls, positive from the bill sleeve's accrual

when_to_use: When the mandate is capital preservation with optional upside - after a large drawdown, during a period the system is not permitted to carry equity risk, or as the default parking structure between strategies. It is the cleanest expression of 'risk only the carry'.
entry_rules: Sleeve instrument must be SGOV, BIL or an equivalent sub-1-year Treasury ETF - not an intermediate bond fund, whose duration would break the capital guarantee.
Call premium budget = sleeve value x current 3-month T-bill yield x (DTE/365). Never exceed it; if the budget buys less than one contract, buy a call debit spread or wait.
Call delta 0.45-0.60, DTE 90-365, on SPY or QQQ only. IV rank <= 50 at purchase - do not spend the whole year's carry on expensive vol.
Total premium at risk per year <= 5% of equity.
Long calls only: no short legs anywhere in this structure, which is what makes it level 2.
management_rules: Take profit at 100% gain on a call by selling it and returning the proceeds to the sleeve; buy the next cycle's call from the next period's interest, never from principal.
Roll the call at 45 DTE if it is still OTM and the remaining premium is more than 25% of the original - otherwise let it expire worthless, which is the budgeted outcome.
Rebalance the sleeve back to 90-95% of equity monthly.
Never average down by buying more calls after a loss; the budget is per period, not per view.
exit_rules: Close every long call at least 2 trading days before expiration - never allow auto-exercise, which would buy 100 shares of SPY (about $60k) against a cash sleeve.
Sell the call immediately if it goes deep ITM with delta >= 0.90 and extrinsic < $0.20 - at that point it is a share proxy, not an option, and carries exercise risk.
Liquidate the sleeve only to meet a real cash need, never to fund an option purchase.
assignment_risk: None from short legs - there are none. The only stock-delivery risk is auto-exercise of a long ITM call at expiry, which the two-day close rule eliminates.
buying_power: Cash for the sleeve plus the call premium. No margin, no short-option requirement.
liquidity_needs: SGOV/BIL are penny-wide; SPY and QQQ LEAPS are the most liquid long-dated options available.
common_mistakes: Funding the calls from principal after a losing cycle, which destroys the whole premise; using an intermediate-duration bond fund as the sleeve; letting an ITM call auto-exercise into a stock position the account cannot carry.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - the structure is an allocation, not a trade.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
